Telesat Lightspeed & Eutelsat OneWeb – Public PDF Specification & Technical Document Links

Compiled: October 25, 2026. Scope: Public PDF documents (and, where no PDF exists or downloads are blocked, direct document or record pages, labelled as such) with technical specifications for (A) Telesat's Lightspeed LEO constellation and its earlier LEO Phase 1 (LEO 1) and LEO 3 test satellites, and (B) the Eutelsat OneWeb LEO constellation (Gen1, Gen1 continuity and next-gen/"Eutelsat Next"), its user terminals and gateways (SNPs). No Telesat GEO-only documents were included. Note: OneWeb merged with Eutelsat in September 2023 and now operates as Eutelsat OneWeb (Eutelsat Group). U.S. filings still use the licensee name WorldVu Satellites Limited, and the UK licensee is Network Access Associates Ltd.

Verification: Every link was checked on Oct 25, 2026. Direct PDFs were confirmed with curl (HTTP 200 and a real %PDF file, page count read). FCC.report, Ofcom and FCC ELS block scripted downloads, so those links were checked by fetching their content or record. Dead links (e.g., two Telesat investor-deck URLs that now return 404) were dropped. "Mirror" marks an exact copy of a filing or datasheet hosted by a third party (FCC.report, resellers). The six shared academic comparisons cover both operators, so they appear in both parts.

Gaps & notes

  • Telesat terminals: no Lightspeed-specific user-terminal datasheets are public yet. Intellian (flat-panel and dual-parabolic reference UTs), Viasat, Farcast, QEST, ALL.SPACE and AvL are named only in web pages and press releases. ThinKom's Ka2517 is the only partner datasheet found, and it is a generic multi-orbit sheet. No FCC ID filings exist for Lightspeed UTs.
  • Telesat LEO 1 (Phase 1) and LEO 3 test satellites: no FCC experimental (ELS) or ISED licence PDFs were found. LEO 3 operated under Telesat's Canadian ITU filings. Only SSTL press-release PDFs and Telesat/ESA web pages describe them. The ESA STARE paper on LEO 3 5G-NTN signals is paywalled (IEEE NAVITEC 2024) and was not included.
  • Telesat FCC: the 2023 amendment to 300 satellites (SAT-APL-20231026-00264) and the 2022 PPL filing are summarised in the FCC public notice, but no stable FCC.report record for the amendment's technical attachment could be confirmed. FCC ICFS / licensing.fcc.gov direct downloads block scripted access, so FCC.report mirrors are used.
  • Telesat investor: the Nov 2024 and May 2026 investor-presentation URLs found in search now return 404 and were dropped. The FY2025 Form 20-F exists only as SEC HTML (not PDF), so the FY2024 20-F PDF is listed instead.
  • ISED Canada publishes only HTML lists for Lightspeed authorizations. No ISED Lightspeed licence or technical-brief PDF is public. ITU EPFD results PDFs for CANSAT-LEO / TELSTAR-LEO or OneWeb L5 / L7A could not be located (the ITU EPFD directory returns 403). Ofcom states the ITU findings were favourable.
  • An earlier note listed "SAT-MOD-20260703-00275 Gen2_MOD" as a OneWeb Gen2 filing. Checking showed it is a SpaceX Gen2 filing, so it was excluded. OneWeb's real next-gen U.S. filing is the 2026 "Eutelsat Next" petition (SAT-PDR/LOA-20260615-00239). Its PDFs are listed on FCC.report as "pending archive", so the document record is linked.
  • Terminal FCC IDs: only Intellian (grantee XXZ) OneWeb terminals have FCC equipment authorizations with test reports. Hughes HL1100W/HL1120W, Kymeta u8 and Stellar Blu terminals are covered by Part 25 licensing. Their only FCC IDs are Wi-Fi/LTE modules (e.g., the Kymeta 2A8PR-HW3 radio; the HL1120W-IDU Wi-Fi router is an Arcadyan module), so they were not listed.
  • Kongsberg and Kontron: no OneWeb-specific datasheet PDFs were found. Kongsberg used Kymeta Peregrine u8 in its OneWeb trials, and Kontron's aero modem/server material does not identify a OneWeb terminal. ThinKom's Ku3030 (2Ku) OneWeb upgrade is mentioned only in news, and its datasheet lists GEO only.
  • OneWeb gateways (SNPs): the 2018 Talkeetna narrative is the only gateway technical PDF that could be verified. Other U.S. SNP (SES-LIC) and international gateway licences exist but were not confirmed with stable links.
  • No OneWeb Gen1 satellite (Airbus/OneWeb Satellites) bus datasheet is public. Satellite-level specs come from FCC narratives, Eutelsat investor documents and ITU/conference decks.
